canonical_rule: docs/model-atlas.json is the single canonical machine model. docs/MODEL-ATLAS.md (generated block) and docs/model-atlas.html (embedded data block) are regenerated from it by scripts/check_model_atlas.py --write and drift-checked by --check. Code is the authority for what is implemented; the checker fails when the atlas and code disagree.

modeled.documented: Implementation contract documented in REPRESENTATION-MAP / INGESTION-DESIGN / CHECKPOINT / SOURCE-AUDIT, in a decision recorded in QUEUE, or in a cited external repository; not in SPEC-v0.2.
modeled.proposed: Proposed by this atlas; needs a decision recorded in QUEUE before implementation.

implemented.none: No table, edge type, view or code exists.
implemented.schema: Table or edge type exists in schema/registry, but no code writes rows. Empty by construction.

populated.none: No rows observed in any exercised input.
populated.synthetic: Rows observed only from synthetic engineering fixtures (in memory).
populated.sample: Rows observed from small retained real samples (in memory); not a corpus.
populated.corpus: Rows observed in a persisted, scoped real snapshot and cited in corpus_evidence (snapshot ID, table or edge kind, count, observer); --runtime re-reads the cited manifest or edge Parquet. The pilot snapshots are hash-ordered cohorts and selections, not the full corpus. Only table-backed entries and model.EDGE_TYPES edges can reach this level; views, columns and view-derived edges stay at their in-memory level.

verified.unit: Covered by in-memory unit tests in a recorded passing run at the baseline commit (verification_runs).
verified.disk: Covered by gated disk tests in a recorded passing run at the baseline commit. If no backing run was read back by the parent or the atlas worker, the level renders as "disk (UNVERIFIED)".
verified.reviewed: Accepted by an independent review (reviewed_by cites a reviews/ file) with no open findings. Nothing is at this level.

rules: verified != none requires implemented != none and at least one tests/ evidence reference.
Planned/proposed entries are never loaded data; zero rows in schema-only tables mean the layer is unavailable, not that the corpus lacks it.
verified unit/disk requires a passing verification run at baseline_commit; verified disk must name it in verified_by.
populated corpus requires corpus_evidence; unknown evidence is never success.
Static analysis that cannot resolve a manifest, rights or edge registry fails the check unless a fingerprinted static contract is declared.

entries.label: Snapshot publication ledger (.publication-ledger.jsonl)
entries.summary: Append-only publication ledger under an exclusive lock (cuneiform/publication.py, format 2). Writers fsync a `reserve` (binding manifest_sha256 and the manifest.json bytes) before the rename, then a `commit`; interrupted publications fail closed until an explicit publication-recover. Guarantee: an ID that was ever published is never served or published with other bytes, for cooperating writers on one host. Accepted at 63f4221 for the authorized local cooperating-writer pilot by the independent final review (reviews/corpus-pilot-review-v0.3.md, review c5df3251): R1-R5 closed. Not proven beyond that scope.
entries.provenance: Added after the same-ID rebuild incident (UI review F-4): at ~09:44Z on 2026-11-03 snapshots ce127437 and 84971360 were published, deleted at ~09:46Z and rebuilt under the same IDs. First-version bytes were not retained, and no copy of them is known. Incident record: ~/.local/share/cuneiform-research/evidence/incident-2026-11-03-same-id-rebuild.json. Both IDs are kept and listed as incident in corpus_snapshots; they are never evidence.
entries.coverage: Seven rows at 63f4221 (read by the atlas worker; ledger SHA-256 6d359b74… is unchanged since 94af111): five legacy rows backfilled at ~09:59Z (two carry the incident note) and one reserve plus one commit for snapshot:5e51403b at 10:36:22Z. Readers label the five ledgered-legacy-backfilled; their published_at is the manifest build time copied by the backfill, and their manifest.json file bytes are not bound (canonical digest only). derived/cohorts has no ledger or lock yet: its three cohorts read as unledgered-pre-ledger-cohort-store. Building any new cohort there creates the cohort ledger, after which those three are refused until the owner adopts them (writer statement, not done). Rows are file entries, not table rows, so populated stays none.
entries.uncertainty: Q-005 blockers at d6049e2: B1 crash window after the rename allowed a same-ID republish; B2 reads never consulted the ledger; B3 failed-publish cleanup masked the error. Q-020 (reviews/corpus-pilot-review-v0.2.md) closed B1 and B3 at 94af111 and kept B2 open on its R1 (a symlinked store entry served as standalone-not-ledger-checked), with R2 (cohort reads), R3 (reserve->commit window), R4 (untyped absent entries) and R5 (seal fsync order). Accepted at 63f4221 for the authorized local cooperating-writer pilot by the independent final review (reviews/corpus-pilot-review-v0.3.md, review c5df3251): R1-R5 closed. Not proven beyond that scope. Writer changes: store membership from the lexical and resolved parent; symlinked or escaping entries, payload symlinks and misplaced IDs refused with symlinked-entry or misplaced before hashing; StoreEntry reads always ledger=require with expected_sid; a writer that finds reserved waits on the per-ID build lock; typed refusals for absent entries; seal fsyncs after the final modes. fsync_dir still ignores OSError. Limits stated by the protocol: cooperating writers on one host; same-owner edits, ledger deletion and root are not prevented; symlink checks are time-of-read; the ledger is not a signature. Open, non-blocking (v0.3 §9): N1 a reader refusal inside a live reserve window says the writer is gone (wording; the read still fails closed); N2 API cohort reads default to auto and label pre-ledger cohorts standalone (wording); N3 publication-clean-stage is guarded by age only. Not tested: same-owner tampering, root, multi-host, real power loss (crashes are process kills).
entries.versioning: Format 1: legacy rows with no event key (the d6049e2 publisher and the 2026-11-03 backfill of the five pilot snapshots), read as published. Format 2 (94af111): reserve, commit, abort, abandon, adopt and torn-tail-acknowledged events; 63f4221 adds no event kind. The cohort ledger under derived/cohorts uses the same format, reached through publication-* --store cohorts. Historical rows are never rewritten. The checker reads both formats itself (corpus-evidence-reader-1).

entries.label: TD-1 Year numbering and BCE convention
entries.summary: Store parsed absolute years as astronomical integers (1 BCE = 0); display BCE/CE; keep the verbatim string and the source era convention.
entries.recommendation: Option 1. Catalog 'BC' years convert as astronomical = 1 − BC year; record era_convention='BC-historical'.

entries.recommendation: Option 1, optionally serializable to EDTF later. Widening rules would be invented precision.

decision_record.choice: Option 1 with precision as-printed/unknown added (Q-004 F8): explicit bounds and precision, ca. flags without widening, ff. opens the end, no midpoints or default day/month.
decision_record.escalate_if: a default ChronologyScheme, a calendar-conversion authority, or any departure from this choice is proposed. Unresolved historical chronology stays source-qualified, never guessed.

entries.label: TD-3 Period labels and chronologies
entries.summary: A period label is a namespaced term. A range printed by the source (e.g. '(ca. 3200-3000 BC)') becomes a source-attributed approximate extent. Any other label→interval mapping is a derived claim citing a ChronologyScheme.
options: Source-printed ranges only + cited schemes as derived claims (recommended)
entries.recommendation: Option 1. No default chronology; competing schemes coexist.

decision_record.choice: Option 1: source-printed ranges only (basis catalog-period-gloss, precision as-printed); no default chronology.
decision_record.escalate_if: a default ChronologyScheme, a calendar-conversion authority, or any departure from this choice is proposed. Unresolved historical chronology stays source-qualified, never guessed.

entries.label: TD-4 Native calendars
entries.summary: Regnal year/month/day formulas and era-based dates are stored as structured native values. Julian conversion only as a derived claim citing a conversion authority; no Gregorian by default.
options: Native value + optional cited conversion claim (recommended)
entries.recommendation: Option 1. Conversion requires an explicit, versioned authority and is never silent.

decision_record.choice: Option 1: native values only; no conversion authority adopted, so no conversion claims are produced.
decision_record.escalate_if: a default ChronologyScheme, a calendar-conversion authority, or any departure from this choice is proposed. Unresolved historical chronology stays source-qualified, never guessed.

entries.label: TD-5 Sentinels and system-date formats
entries.summary: '00.00.00.00', empty strings and 'None' are unknown, not dates. Ambiguous system dates (e.g. '12/4/2001') parse only under a declared per-source format; otherwise raw only.
entries.recommendation: Option 1; heuristic parsing would invent month/day order.

decision_record.choice: Option 1: sentinels and empty strings are unknown; system dates parse only under a declared per-source format.
decision_record.escalate_if: a default ChronologyScheme, a calendar-conversion authority, or any departure from this choice is proposed. Unresolved historical chronology stays source-qualified, never guessed.

entries.label: TD-6 Bitemporal separation
entries.summary: Valid time (what the source asserts about the past) is separate from knowledge time (snapshot that contains the assertion) and processing time (manifests/receipts). Timestamps never enter IDs.
options: Snapshot as knowledge-time boundary + manifest times (recommended)
entries.recommendation: Option 1: consistent with immutable snapshots; per-row timestamps would break deterministic IDs/hashes.

decision_record.choice: Option 1: snapshot is the knowledge-time boundary; processing time stays in manifests and receipts.
decision_record.escalate_if: a default ChronologyScheme, a calendar-conversion authority, or any departure from this choice is proposed. Unresolved historical chronology stays source-qualified, never guessed.

entries.summary: Every dating is a separate attributed DateClaim in the claim table (predicate 'dated_to', TemporalExtent in details), linked via CLAIM_SUBJECT. Queries return all with attribution; no winner is chosen.
options: Reuse claim table with typed details (recommended)
entries.recommendation: Option 1 first; promote to a typed table only if query needs justify it. Columns on artifact would force a single winner.

decision_record.choice: Option 1: reuse the claim table with typed details; no winner is chosen.
